findings.message: Acceptance criterion 3 is not met. The file has no test for drain startup reconciliation, reconciliation after each dispatch, the configured private SubprocessNotifications transport, or the unset-notify warn-once, status-only path. The Drain(reconcile_notifications=...) wiring in squatch/__main__.py and squatch/drain.py is not exercised by any test in the diff.
findings.paved_road: Add tests to tests/test_watchdog_activation.py that run the real _drain root through main(['drain']) with an injected process and clock. They should assert: reconcile runs before the first dispatch and after every dispatch; a configured notify uses a SubprocessNotifications whose env has no provider auth keys; and an unset notify prints the warning once and sends nothing.

findings.message: Acceptance criterion 1 requires driving the real bootstrap drain and serve composition. The activation test calls compose_pipeline(watchdog=True) directly, so it bypasses the _locked/_drain/_serve roots that set watchdog. Nothing proves that drain actually binds the wrapper. Serve is only covered by a monkeypatched isinstance check in tests/test_watchdog.py.
findings.paved_road: Drive main(['drain']) and main(['serve']) in tests/test_watchdog_activation.py with an injected process that emits stream-json events and an injected clock. Assert that Implement and Review calls reach the detector and produce the watchdog signal for the correct ticket and run_seq through both roots.

findings.message: Acceptance criterion 2 requires proof that the stuck path still aborts and unwinds. test_stuck_signal_is_ticket_wide_and_wrapper_delegates_abort only checks the signal body, then calls subject.abort_current() by hand. It never shows LLMEffect's stuck_seconds timeout aborting a hanging call through WatchdogLLM, cleaning up the process group and unwinding the Stages run.
findings.paved_road: Add a test that builds the composed pipeline with watchdog=True and a process that hangs past ticket.stuck_minutes under the injected clock. Assert that LLMEffect aborts through WatchdogLLM.abort_current and reaches CliClient.abort_current, that the stuck signal is appended once with the specified body, and that the run unwinds the way it did before this change.

findings.message: Output mutations are observed through `git status` in the finally of _call, after the LLM call has finished. The implementer commits its changes (the test's StageProcess does too), so committed fence edits never show in porcelain status and never reset detector spend. That makes a productive run look like spend without progress. The ticket asks for mutation observations through the filesystem seam, not a git status sweep. Also, an exception raised by the awaited git.status inside finally (for example, a workspace that was removed or broken during abort) replaces the original exception from the driver.
findings.paved_road: Observe mutations during the run, not afterwards. Either route worktree writes through the WatchdogFilesystem seam, or compute changes against the run's base commit (for example, diff names base...HEAD plus the worktree) so committed work counts. Do not let the observation raise out of the finally block.
